Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from here. We are done with the warm-ups. Now it is time for the big event. We have a day's rest and we will meet on 30th May, 2019 for Match 1 between England and South Africa at The Oval, London at 1030 local (0930 GMT). For now, goodbye.

Windies skipper, Jason Holder, says it is a good win and he hopes it is building towards something special in the World Cup. Mentions Gayle gave them the impetus they needed at the start and the rest did exceptionally well. Further adds he is pleased with the bowlers and how they stuck to the plans. States there were a few blunders towards the end in the field but overall they had a good game. Tells they need to pay more attention to their fielding. Ends by saying they just want to enjoy their cricket in the World Cup and see where it takes them.

New Zealand, Kane Williamson, he thought the exercise today was outstanding, they know what the Windies are capable of and they showed their power today. Mentions they expect their bowling attack to be under pressure throughout the tournament and today was a good learning curve but not everyday can be their day. Credits Tom Blundell for the way he played, it was a knock under pressure and he did really well. States he can't reveal the information of whether they will play Blundell in the first game or not but he is happy with how he played.

Tom Blundell who is up for an interview, says he feels very good, it was a great day for him and he is happy he got a ton. States he is happy to spend some time out in the middle. Further adds the last few days have been good, they have had two good games and they are looking forward to the game against Lanka. Mentions he just backed his ability and he is confident when he goes out to bat. He is hopeful of getting a chance in the World Cup. Tells he has still no idea about his inclusion in the XI for the first game but he is happy if he plays or not. Ends by saying the target was always going to be a tough one and he is pleased with how they finished in the end.

The Windies bowling was very good to begin with. Till the time the ball was new, Cottrell, Thomas and Holder, all did a good job. However, once the ball got soft, their bowlers did take a pounding. Only Nurse was able to bowl a good spell during the middle overs. Carlos Brathwaite though finished as the pick of the bowlers as he ended with a three-fer.

A comfortable win for the Windies! An absolute morale boosting one for them. After Shai Hope's ton and handy innings from Lewis and Russell, they posted a massive 422. In reply, New Zealand needed a powerful start but they did not get it. They lost three even before they got to 50. Williamson and Blundell then steadied the ship. The two added a 120-run stand but just as they started to get going, the skipper got run out. Blundell then came out of his shell though, he started playing lovely shots, smashed the bowlers out of the park and got to a ton. However, the task was too much of an ask and once he fell, it was all about playing out the 50 overs for the Kiwis which they did.

OUT! RUN OUT! The last thing New Zealand would have wanted at the moment, that too, it is their skipper who is taking the long walk back. The partnership had started to get going and a mix-up spoils it. First, Blundell plays a lovely dab down towards third man. Allen from short third man hares after it. The batsmen take two. Blundell is charging for the first and second run but Williamson is seen jogging. Allen in the meantime, pushes the ball back in play before it crosses the ropes. Williamson then senses an opportunity for the third and goes for it. Blundell too goes for it but Kane then realizes he is in trouble and stops, so does Tom but then Williamson continues. Till then, the ball gets to the keeper who collects it and whips the bails off. KW is well short. There always going to be a run out when the batsmen hesitated in the middle but it was Williamson who sacrificed his wicket. A fine innings by Kane comes to an end. Hats off to Williamson though! He could have easily turned around and gone back to his end which means Blundell would have been the one to have got out. But he knew it was his mistake and he did not want TB to pay the price. Speaks volumes about the captaincy quotient and teammate quotient in that man.

Good length delivery coming in towards the stumps, Taylor does well to keep it out to mid on.
Taylor display a solid front foot defense to this length ball from Holder.
Length delivery on off, Williamson plays it to point. Wicket maiden over from Kemar Roach. This is excellent bowling from him.
On a good length on middle, Kane defends it out.
Good length delivery on off, the skipper defends it off the front foot.
BEATEN! On a good length and outside off, Williamson looks to defend but misses it due to the away movement on this one.
Ross Taylor is the new man in!

OUT! New Zealand lose their second wicket and are in deep trouble now. Roach bowls a good short ball, Nicholls looks to pull but gets a top edge. Henry wanted to drag it. It goes towards Holder who runs from mid on and takes a comfortable catch. West Indies are right in the game now.
APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! On a good length on leg, Nicholls looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head.
Kemar Roach is on!
Williamson leaves this length ball outside off easily for the keeper.
Kane defends this outside off delivery off the back foot near the pitch on the off side.
Henry Plays this good length delivery outside off with an open face towards point. Where the fielder makes a half stop and the batsman sneak in a single.
Henry defends this length ball pitching outside off towards point.
Henry defends this good length ball back to bowler off the back foot.
Length delivery on pads, flicked straight to mid-wicket fielder.

FOUR! Excellent shot from the skipper. Short and outside off, Williamson cuts it through point for a boundary. 7 runs and a wicket from the over. The West Indies have got the crucial wicket of Martin Guptill.
On a length on leg, Nicholls nudges it towards square leg for a run.
Length delivery on middle, Nicholls flicks it through mid-wicket. The batsmen get two runs.
Kane Williamson is the new batsman in.

OUT! First breakthrough for West Indies. Cottrell bowls a good short ball on middle, Guptill looks to pull but gets a top edge. It goes towards mid-wicket where Darren Bravo takes a good catch running backwards. Not the start New Zealand would have wanted.
Play and a miss! On a good length and outside off, Guptill looks to drive but misses it due to the away swing on this one.
Bowls a bouncer on leg, Guptill does well to duck under it.
Nicholls defends this good length delivery to the off side.
FOUR! Length ball outside off, Henry sees the width and cuts it powerfully through square on the off side and the ball races away to the fence in no time.

Had the fielder from point hit Henry was a Gonner! Guptill drops this length ball towards point and calls his partner for a quick single. Henry responds to it, the fielder at point dives and fires in a throw at the striker's end but misses it.

BEATEN! This time Holder beats the outside edge of Guptill. He bowls a length ball outside off and Guptill looks to defend off the front foot but gets beaten on the outside edge. Guptill living dangerously here.
Vicious bounce! Holder makes the ball jump from a length. Guptill was lining to defend it but seeing the ball rise, drops his wrists just in time and sways away from the line of the delivery.
Henry just flicks this length ball on the stumps to the mid-wicket region to bring Guptill on strike.
FOUR! Excellent shot. Full and outside off, Guptill drives it through wide mid off for a boundary. 6 runs have come from the over.
Good length delivery on off, Guptill plays it to off side.
On a good length on off, Martin defends it off the front foot.
Well bowled by Sheldon Cottrell. This came back in. Full on middle, Guptill drives it to mid on.
Full on middle, Guptill drives it to mid on.
Length delivery on off, Nicholls looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards slip where it falls short of the fielder. The batsmen take a run.
WIDE! Cottrell has conceded three wides already and this is his fourth. Bowls it wide and outside off, Nicholls lets it go.
Guptill defends this length delivery to the off side by coming right behind the ball.
Henry flicks this length delivery to the leg side for a single.
This time Holder corrects his line and bowls a length ball outside off, Henry leaves it  for the keeper to do the rest.

FOUR! When the fine leg is up inside the circle, you don't bowl on pads, Holder bowls this delivery on a length and on the pads, Henry flicks it past the short fine leg fielder and here comes the first boundary for New Zealand and Henry.
Henry looks to pull this length ball from holder but gets hit high on the pads off an inside edge.
Holder starts with a length ball on the stumps and Henry plays it down the ground. Stopped by Holder in his followthrough.
Jason Holder to bowl from the other end.
On a length on middle, Guptill flicks it to leg side. Good start from West Indies. Just the 3 extras from the over.
WIDE! Bowls it down the leg side, Guptill looks to play at that but misses it.
Good length delivery on off, Guptill defends it out.
Outside off, Martin shoulders his arms to this one.
The physio is out to have a look! Russell seems to be in a lot of pain. The good news is though, he is fine to continue.
Full on off, Guptill drives it to mid off where Russell does well to field it but gets hurt in the process. He is down on the ground and is in pain. He got hurt in the wrist.

NOT OUT! It is going over! Excellent review by Guptill. It would have been a dreadful start for them as Guptill could play a key role in this chase. This is on a length and around off, it comes back in. Guptill defends outside the line and gets hit on the front pad. An appeal and the umpire raises the finger. Guptill, after a chat with his partner, takes it upstairs. Replays roll in and they show that the ball is going over. The on-field call has to be overturned. Guptill survives to fight another day.
Review time! Guptill has been given out LBW! He has reviewed. Looks out.
Good length delivery outside off, Guptill looks to defend but misses it due to the away movement on this one.
WIDE! Consecutive wides from Sheldon. Bowls it down the leg side, Guptill looks to go after it but misses it.
WIDE! Cottrell starts with a bouncer, Guptill does well to duck under it. First run for New Zealand and they are off the mark.
The Kiwi Opening pair of Martin Guptill and Henry Nicholls will start the Kiwi chase. Sheldon Cottrell will open the bowling for the West Indies.
Welcome back for the chase. The players and the umpires are out in the middle.
